The room was clean and reasonably comfortable, although some parts of the furniture and bathroom felt slightly outdated. The housekeeping staff did a good job maintaining cleanliness throughout our stay. The bed was comfortable enough for a good night’s sleep.

The rooftop area and pool were nice, offering a pleasant view of the ocean. It’s a good place to relax in the evening. However, the pool area can get crowded at times.

Overall, The Kingsbury is a good hotel with a great location and decent facilities. It may not feel extremely luxurious in every aspect, but it provides a comfortable stay in Colombo.

comment:
We visited Kingsbury Harbour Court for the lunch buffet to celebrate my brother’s birthday, and unfortunately the experience was extremely poor from start to finish.

The service was disorganized and unprofessional. When we tried to raise concerns, the manager was standing at the entrance, fully engaged in a conversation with a colleague, completely unaware and unresponsive—even while staff were calling him over for our complaint. When he finally engaged, there was no apology or ownership taken, neither from him nor from the staff.

The dessert counter was almost completely empty (around 90%) and remained that way for over 30 minutes. Even after we complained, it took another 20–30 minutes for items to be refilled. Similarly, at the pasta station, prawns were not refilled for over 30 minutes. Guests were expected to “adjust” due to poor organization in the kitchen, which is unacceptable at this level.

Food quality and hygiene were also major concerns. Several counters had long hair visibly present in the food. And the pasta counter Chef gives excuses as to saying it's guests. Where is the Hygiene and Safety Manager? The spread itself was extremely limited, with hardly any meat options. Dumplings were unavailable, and staff were unable to explain properly—one staff member rudely said “only one is available” without any clarity or courtesy.

The Thai noodle station was particularly disappointing—the staff member focused more on theatrics than actual cooking quality. At the pork station, one staff member appeared more interested in flirting with a colleague than attending to guests and disappeared after serving one portion. Despite seeing many chefs in the back, there was no coordination or efficiency.

The complimentary birthday cake, which was mentioned as part of the celebration, was later charged.

While a few waiters and hostesses were polite and helpful, overall the team lacked professionalism and proper training, especially in handling guest complaints. Staff simply ran to managers instead of listening or resolving issues—and unfortunately, management itself was a major letdown.

I rarely complain. I usually observe and guide, as I am a General Manager myself at a Marriott property. However, this experience was far below any acceptable hospitality standard. Even when compared to other local hotel buffets, this was one of the worst experiences.

I would not recommend Harbour Court to anyone, and I will not be returning.

To add to the disappointment, imagine having to pay for a “complimentary” birthday cake, and only having a single staff member acknowledge the celebration, no basic gesture, nothing but charged for a complimentary cake. At other hotels such as Shangri-La or ITC, even a minimal effort is made to recognize special occasions with a few team members singing along with you. Here, there was complete indifference. Honestly, it feels like it’s time for Kingsbury to consider handing this Hotel over to an international chain and building a proper service culture, because the current setup is chaotic. If a manager is unable to handle or even acknowledge a guest complaint, what can one realistically expect from the rest of the team? At one point, I asked a staff member who was serving water for a spoon—he disappeared for nearly an hour. I had to ask another staff member, who finally brought it. This level of basic service failure is unacceptable.

comment:
The Kingsbury has really lost its charm, and it’s sad to see how much the quality has dropped over the years. This used to be one of the go-to places for cakes or high tea in Colombo, but now it’s completely the opposite. I honestly wouldn’t recommend it anymore—not even as a last resort.

Their so-called "Tiramisu High Tea" was one of the worst I’ve ever experienced. Almost everything was labeled “Tiramisu,” yet hardly anything tasted like it. They had “Tiramisu Date Pudding,” “Tiramisu Ice Cream,” and even a “Tiramisu Matcha Ice Cream” and so much more that just had crushed ladyfingers thrown in. One chef even insisted that “anything with ladyfingers counts as Tiramisu,” which shows just how little they understand about it. Out of the whole spread, only one dessert labeled 'Classic Tiramisu' carried a slight coffee flavor and came somewhat close to the real thing. The savory items were okay, but when you advertise a themed tea, it shouldn’t be carried by just one halfway-decent dessert.

The space itself is another problem in this hotel. The hall is so small and gets extremely overcrowded, especially in the hallways, making the whole experience feel chaotic and uncomfortable. On top of that, the service was disappointing—despite having a reservation, our table wasn’t ready, and we had to wait. To make things worse, some staff members were unprofessional, even trying to flirt with guests and asking for personal details while serving at the buffet. That kind of behavior is completely unacceptable for a hotel of this standard.

The cakes weren’t any better. We recently bought the Almond Cake and Oreo Cake, and both were terrible. The Almond Cake tasted like raw margarine with no almond flavor other than a few flakes stuck around it, and it left such a bad aftertaste that we had to throw it away. The Oreo Cake didn’t taste like Oreo at all, and both sponge cakes had the texture of rubber.

On top of all this, the staff seemed uninterested in guest feedback and lacked even basic cutlery etiquette.

The Kingsbury used to be a name people trusted for quality, but now it’s overcrowded, overpriced, and poorly managed. Sadly, it’s no longer worth the time, or money.

comment:
Well planned family dinner with a Toddler - Ruined

I booked the dinner buffet for last Sunday dinner. In my first call I informed there will be 5 adults and a 3 year old toddler. Then the operator clearly told me the seating will be 6. (of cause it has to be we do not go to a 5 star hotel and keep our baby in the lap )
I requested a seating near the window since it'll be easy to keep the toddler distracted. I also requested 3x3 seating since our toddler behaves well while seated in between his parents.

The operator said in the call that she have put a special note with this info

I did this booking on Friday. On Saturday the baby's father informed me recently they went to the same buffet and they faced an unpleasant situ.  Once they went to the buffet there was no baby chair to the baby and staff said they should have specially requested for the chair - just informing we have toddler is not enough. and they got a baby chair with a little hustle.

Therefore I called again to make sure I mentioned the Baby chair.
during that call I again made sure the special note is there and operator reconfirmed me the details.

On Sunday I got two calls to reconfirm the booking from the Hotel(A guy and then a girl after approximately two hours apart). checked if the details are correct with them both time.

Finally when we arrived around 7.00pm. voilà.!!

-- A tiny female staff came, checked the booking by name, escorted us to a seating by window seat of 5 seating (No room for the baby)
-- Told her that's not the booking requested -  puzzled and annoyed face was shown to us.
-- Then she escorted us to a six seating 3*3 after I explained verbally (the employee not referring to the notes they took via calls) - this time no window seating.
-- I had to tell her that a six seating 3*3 window seating  was what requested;

*******
The staff told me I must have not communicated properly. I told her I did and also reconfirmed in the following calls. shook her head dismissing my claim. I requested her to refer the special note in the booking. she said she checked and there wasn't anything like that. I MUST NOT HAVE TOLD THEM IN WHEN MAKING THE BOOKING..!!!

At this point I was loosing my temper and I told her my calls are getting recorded and invited her to listen to them and show me in their booking system that there is no such information recorded as she's claiming (lying literally)

Mind you at least three 3*3 six person window seating  arrangements were vacant in the premises when this drama was unfolding.

Finally we were escorted to one of them with sour faced staff and baby chair arrived after reminding two three times.. :)

Poor food spread - details below

We had to wave like refugees for water refills since waiting staff just pass by without noticing when we wave.

The Cherry on top of the cake was one the staff who involved in the seating drama asking me if I enjoy their "service".

I wonder if these employees are bribed by rival hotels since  cinnamon lakeside/ life COD cuz we were all regretting not going there spending little extra and receive better service and food spread.

I've been to this place since it was Ceylon Continental, After rebranding to Kingsbury, to High tea, brunch, bar, Honey Beach many times and had a lot of pleasant memories here. but will never choose this place unless I'm a guest of someone else who chose this place.

I'm questioning the management on:

- Why your staff not attending the booking requirements made while making the appointment.???
- Why don't they read the special notes in the bookings?
- Why they are not asking the golden question if the guests need a baby chair for the baby when they mention there is a baby among the guests?? if they have a policy of only providing it on prior request?
- Why your Sunday  international dinner buffet don't have the must have staples like lamb, blue cheese. the cashew curry in Sri Lankan cuisine?

This will be the end of my visits to once glorious Kingsbury...!!

Never again..!!

We paid LKR 4,700 per person for six people—this was not a casual meal or a discounted offer. It was a special treat for a once-in-a-lifetime occasion. I trusted Kingsbury to deliver a premium experience. Instead, we were met with poor service, disorganized staff, and unprofessional behavior.

From the moment we walked in, the experience was uncomfortable. The staff member at the restaurant entrance, Achini, greeted us with zero warmth or professionalism. Beyond luxury, you need more…
I stayed at this hotel in Colombo on March 6th. I arrived, had a free day with dinner included, and was scheduled to leave the next day at 6:00 AM for the airport.
Knowing I couldn't have breakfast sitting down, I asked my guide if it was possible to get a simple breakfast box to take away. Nothing complicated, just a few things to avoid leaving on an empty stomach. The answer? No need, you can easily have breakfast at 6:00 AM and leave at 6:15 AM. This is what the older gentleman at the reception desk assured me.
Unfortunately, the next morning, at 6:00 AM, I went downstairs and was met by two young men who informed me that breakfast wasn't served before 6:30 AM. I explained the situation to the translator, but a sort of "press conference" ensued between them. After five minutes, they finally led me to the buffet, where I asked for a simple coffee and milk. At that point, they looked at each other as if I'd asked for oysters and caviar.
The result? I grab a measly muffin and leave, bidding a hearty goodbye.
Now, I'd like to point out a few things:
1. Breakfast was paid for.
2. If you can't even organize that, imagine the rest.
3. Good heavens, you don't work at NASA!
Finally, a little advice: with the prices you charge, you could at least hire someone who speaks a few words of Italian. Because in Sri Lanka, even in the most remote places, you can find someone who speaks it. Except at your hotel.
Obviously, I won't recommend this property and I'll certainly never return.

Luxury is not enough…

They were shouting without any discipline and rudely asked me to move. It was very uncomfortable. Is that what hospitality looks like in a star-class hotel? We felt like we were in a street restaurant.

After that, we returned to our table. When my other friends arrived with a cake, no one provided a knife or a side plate until we asked for it. We did not expect such poor service from a hotel of this standard.

To make matters worse, all our drinks got caught in the rain, and instead of replacing them immediately, they brought the drinks now mixed with rainwater back to our table. Can anyone drink that? We had to ask for new drinks, and only then did they provide them.

However, I want to appreciate one lady who helped us dry our clothes .her service was commendable.

I’m also a hotelier, which is why we chose this venue for such a special occasion, but it turned out to be the worst experience we’ve had at a star-class hotel. There were so many staff members in full suits perhaps managers but what’s the point of having them if they don’t lead their team or step in when guests are facing issues?

Why should we spend our money on this kind of service? But the food was very good.

comment:
I recently stayed at this beautiful and luxurious hotel that everyone raves about in the city and I definitely wanted to check it out myself. I travelled from Galle and pampered myself to a two night stay at The Kingsbury.

The hotel is grand and very welcoming to smiling faces of staff working there and showering their warm hospitality upon everyone. The hotel was busy which was great for the business and team were on their toes to ensure a great experience for everyone staying or visiting.

Coming to the positives -

1. Food was outstanding everywhere. Tried 4-5 outlets throughout the stay and the food and hospitality at the F&B outlets was divine specially at Yue Chuan and Tenku. The F&B team was great and chefs really definitely did put their heart and soul into the cooking.

2. Spa at the hotel was amazing. Really professional therapists and the team at the reception was truly welcoming and ensured a great experience during the therapies. I did have a suggestion and have already mentioned it to the spa team and that is to keep some loofahs at the spa on request for those guests to do choose to take a shower there itself.

3. Gymnasium was well equipped and definitely maintained to a great standard.

Unfortunately there were a few hiccups as well.

1. First and foremost , I was actually given a key to an occupied room on arrival. The guest occupying the room was lady and she was getting her makeup done when I walked in assuming she must be at the hotel for an event. However it was very embarrassing for both of us as she was in the middle of getting ready and I just invaded her privacy unknowingly. I definitely apologised for the inconvenience and went back to the reception and did let the team know. They mentioned that due to Houskeeping’s negligence, the room was marked ready as per their system. I hope they did speak to the guest and made sure everything was fine ! It was surely a very big inconvenience to the guest occupying the room and myself ! Unfortunately nothing was done post that by the team with regard to the same.

2. I had placed my order for lunch through room service upon arrival in the new room however the team member who delivered the food requested for the payment to be done at the same time rather than posting it to the room. It was actually the case for all the outlets I visited and none of them billed the checks to the room. Unfortunately not all the in-house guests like to carry their credit cards along to every space of the hotel they visit. Looked quite odd but that might just be the hotel policy unfortunately it was not informed upon arrival.

3. I had placed an order through the beach club for lunch on the day of departure which took about an hour and a half to be delivered to the room. I had reconfirmed with the employee at the beach club about the delivery and he over excitedly mentioned to have it served without an issue within 20-25 minutes. However after two follow-ups once through the reception and second through the room service, the order was finally served.

There were a few ups and downs about The Kingsbury however overall what I had heard off about the service and hospitality unfortunately that little spark was missing which could have definitely elevated the entire stay experience i was hoping for !

We had a very bad experience on our wedding day (14/07/2024) at the Kingsbury Hotel. The front door staff and managers at the Kingsbury started a fight with the Ashtaka service (Charithra Wedding Services). The Kingsbury security didn't allow them to use the front door to enter, and the situation escalated quickly. Our wedding day coordinator from Kingsbury, Shaun Bernard, never mentioned any front door rules to us. If he had, we could have informed Charithra Wedding Services about them.

We faced a similar issue with the marquee letter delivery. Kingsbury didn't allow us to bring them through the front door. Fortunately, my brother was there and carried them all alone through the back door to the wedding hall (Victorian Hall, 10th floor). Our wedding entrance was planned to start at 10:30 am. I (the groom) went to take some photos on the ground floor with my vehicle as requested by the photographers. It was around 10:15 am. As I was nearing the front door, I heard a loud noise and a fight. Initially, I didn't pay much attention as I was in a rush to take photos and go to the 10th floor to start the entrance event. But then I realized that the fight was between the Kingsbury management and the Ashtaka service. The Kingsbury top management was yelling at the Ashtaka person for some reason and asking them to leave the premises. There were only 15 minutes left before the event started. I was exhausted and scared because all our sacrifices for the past two to three months and our wedding day could have been ruined. I begged them to stop the fight and continue the event. We had made full payments to both Kingsbury Hotel and Charithra Wedding Services, yet both acted like children, yelling at each other. Fortunately, the Ashtaka person took a step back and decided to continue the event. I was shaking for another half hour thinking about that even during the Poruwa ceremony. It was the worst experience on our wedding day. The Kingsbury staff was not helpful at all.

The Kingsbury wedding coordinator, Shaun, was either busy or pretended to be busy all the time. He wasn't even present on the wedding day morning at Kingsbury. The wedding hall staff was also not punctual. We asked them to arrange tables and serve dry bites, wedding cakes, and welcome drinks by 10:30 am. I'm posting this to give an idea to couples planning their big day at this hotel. By some luck we're able to lock the door in the other room but it took some time. Even then the bathroom door remains slightly opened (It is a sliding door). Any sound we make can be heard within the whole room so it is quite embarrassing and disturbing. The glass that is supposed to be censoring both sides barely makes any effect. We can still see through them (depends on how far away you are).

-Loud music from bars within the hotel.
As I write this review at night time, there is loud music playing. I am at the 9th floor yet it is that loud. We're a Muslim family and it is hard as we try to pray while we hear the loud music. It is really disturbing for us.

For a 5 star hotel to have these such issues, it is really concerning. I request the management to come up a solution for these problems.

Although, I kind of enjoyed my stay. The staff members were really kind. The pool and sauna was an amazing experience. I hope I get to visit this hotel soon, but this time with my mentioned concerns resolved.

comment:
Im highly disappointment with the experience my family and I encountered at Kingsbury Harbour Court during the dinner buffet on the 3rd of December. We chose your establishment to celebrate my mother's 60th  birthday and unfortunately, the evening fell short of our expectations.

Upon inquiring at the reception about reservations, we were informed of two available time slots, 7 PM and 9 PM. Opting for the latter, we were assured by your staff that the food spread and refilling would be adequately managed.

Upon arrival,we encountered confusion at the appetizer corner where a yellow dish lacked a name tag. One of your assistant chefs initially identified it as pineapple but later contradicted himself by stating it was a fish dish.we were disheartened to find that certain dishes, notably the kottu, were already finished. Only after raising the issue to the manager did we receive attention and the kottu was eventually served at our table. I must commend Chef Sashi Kumar for his prompt action and accommodating demeanor during this incident.

This lack of clarity reflects poorly on the presentation and knowledge of your staff.

Throughout the evening, we had to continually remind the waiters to clear our plates. Furthermore, the cake cutting, an integral part of celebrating my mother's birthday, required three reminders before a waiter hastily delivered the cake without any ceremonial elements. In similar establishments, it is customary for a duty manager to accompany such moments with greetings or music, which unfortunately was absent from our experience.

Despite bringing these concerns to the attention of your Front Desk manager, we have yet to receive any feedback or resolution regarding our complaint.

We arrived at your esteemed establishment expecting a delightful evening to celebrate a special occasion. Regrettably, our experience did not meet the standards one would anticipate from a renowned 5-star hotel.

Thanks

Regards
R.Hettiarachchi
